assumptions_resolved: Admission's GitHub reads were billed to the reviewer operation's derived 25-request budget; suspending accounting around the admission call in place keeps requireOwnedRef mutex-ownership proof intact, which moving the call site would have destroyed.

REVIEW_OPERATION_REQUEST_LIMIT is unchanged at 25 and REVIEW_MUTEX_SECTION_RESERVE is unchanged at 15; the defect was the accounting boundary, not the size of the ceiling. The green-path test still asserts both constants.
Admission still runs, still refuses identically, and still runs under the same held mutex before the reviewer draw.

CORRECTED IN THIS GENERATION (reviewer finding 1): the prose this change added described the old failure as the entry gate refusing BEFORE the mutex was taken. That was wrong and contradicted the same paragraphs' statement that admission runs under the held mutex. The observed order in assignNextReviewerOperation is requireReviewWireCapacity, then acquireReviewMutex, then requirePrOperationRoute -> requireAdmission. The quoted exhaustion message naming the mutex-release reserve is only constructed in consumeReviewWireRequest when the budget is locked and not cleaning up, and acquireReviewMutex is what sets locked and cleanupReserve, so the refusal can only have fired with the mutex already held. Both the doc callout and the comment above withoutReviewRequestBudget now say so.

CORRECTED IN THIS GENERATION (reviewer finding 2): the #2802 green-path test's comments claimed a production-shaped request count. They no longer do. Production githubIo.getFileAt and treeFiles read through laneTreeReader -> createTreeReader in scripts/lib/github-tree.mjs, which calls runGitHubCommand from scripts/lib/github-transport.mjs; that shared transport never calls consumeReviewWireRequest, so blob and tree reads are not charged to the reviewer budget in production. Production admission charges getPr, getPrFiles via ghPaginated, closingIssuesForPr, getIssue and the comment/outcome-history reads. The fixture wires three admission reads onto the budgeted executor deliberately; the test is a revert detector, not a measurement. No assertion was weakened, removed or re-pointed: only comments changed in the test file.
